newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 5.00 cents higher Monday after a strong performance in London overnight, traders said.
LIFFE July robusta futures surged to new contract highs early Monday, but by midday some of the gains were pared. July was up $95 at the break at $2,150 after peaking at $2,190.

The focus this week is likely to be in London, where the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) is meeting to discuss whether to suspend their export quotas to help cool the explosive price rally.
The talks opened with a session of the technical group of Brazil, Colombia, Ivory Coast, Indonesia, Uganda and El Salvador which will put forward proposals for a full meeting on Wednesday.

Friday, New York arabica futures pulled back in a modest correction to last week's sharp run-up. July settled 2.05 cents lower at 253.15 cents after trading from 258.00 to 245.00 cents. Spot May, which set a new lifetime high of 280.00 this morning, fell 0.55 cent to 276.50 cents, while the back months closed down 0.20 to 2.70.

After Friday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 4,500 bags, to 41,682 bags as of May 13. There were 8,405 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after Friday's finish, Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation has decided to reopen May/June coffee registrations for shipments by private exporters to Europe and Japan, more than one month after shutting them down, industry sources said.

A statement from National Coffee Exporters' Association of Colombia (Asoexport) said registrations for the shipment of up to 500,000 60-kg bags of coffee to Europe and Japan in May and June, would be opened to private exporters next week.
